events.title: ECMAScript 5 standard adopted (ECMA-262 5th edition)
events.summary: Ecma approved ECMA-262 5th edition on December 3, 2009 — adding strict mode, JSON, and getters/setters to JavaScript.
events.about: ES5 bridged the long gap between ES3 and ES2015. Strict mode (`"use strict"`) caught common bugs; native `JSON.parse`/`stringify` replaced libraries; getters and setters enabled cleaner object APIs. It was the foundation jQuery-era code built on before transpilers made ES6 mainstream.

narrative.whyChosen: ES5 was the first major JavaScript update in ten years and fixed real-world browser inconsistencies.
narrative.whyImportant: Strict mode and JSON support made large client-side codebases safer without waiting for ES2015.
narrative.problemSolved: The abandoned ES4 effort left the language frozen; ES5 delivered practical improvements browsers could ship quickly.
